posts.author: montehawks
posts.body:
just a small request... i see in visumz core i can set the crisis color... im guessing crisis is 30% or under? i am hoping to find a plugin that will let me change enemy name colors in a couple of different ways. maybe give us an option, or combine both.
1. similar to the everquest con system, against actor in the 1st slot, enemies 1-3 lvls lower would be blue, even lvl white, 1 to 3 higher yellow, and 4 or more would be red. as far as actual implementation, id want something like this;
color (hex):  xxxx
enemy level compared to actor in slot 1: -1 to -3
color (hex): yyyy
enemy level: 0
color (hex): zzzz
enemy level: 1 to 3
etc
2. enemy name colors reflect their health.. in my mind i would like to set a color at every 10% of health, ideally through hex so it can be completely custom. if both could be combined, maybe prioritize this when an enemy is targeted while choosing who to attack over 1. something like
100 health: xxx
90 health: yyy
80 health: zzz
etc
thank you for your time. would be happy to donate as well, to have something like this made.
also, i understand i can use health bars. imo they are kinda jank, i dont like how they look, and they break immersion for the style im going for.

posts.author: Strahl
posts.body:
Here you go I've implemented both into the plugin. The way it behaves now is it changes all enemy names to have the level in their name. You set the enemy's level to the notes section on the enemy database. For example put " <level:15>  "  This will set the enemies level.
For here you will see in battle, The enemy's level text will be blue if they're 3+ levels below yours, it will be yellow if they're between 2 levels lower and 3 levels higher, and then it will be red if they are 4+ levels higher than your party's average level.
Moving onto the HP colors. I've simply coded it to transition from white to red. Every 10% hp, it will get slightly more red.
I will mention, this is made to use rpg maker's default battle systems. I tested it on the side-view ATB version. I can't guarantee it will work with custom battle plugins. Let me know if there are any issues.
I hope you don't mind, but I'm going to post this for others to use as well.

I wasn't expecting someone to tackle this one, let alone so quickly. one thing ended up working for me, and that is the emerge text color coding the mobs, but i dont use the emerge text, i have that turned off.
the battle system i am using is stb / visumz standard turn battle. the gradual shift from 100% to red at 0% did not work.
i am also using visumz enemy levels, so i have a functioning enemy level system thats pretty basic. since i am using custom stats, it doesnt work as far as scaling anything other than health. but the notetag for that is <Level: x to y> or <Level: x>. this also has its own way of labeling enemy names with the level if i want or i can turn it off. right now i have it set as "[Enemy Name] - [Level: Enemy Level]"... however, the goal of the plugin for me would be to get rid of the level label entirely, and it only be the color of the names as indicators to the player at how strong or weak the enemy might be.
if its hard to make a completely custom one where i can edit the information myself, i am looking for this color scheme,
10+ levels under group - gray
5-10 levels under group - light blue
1 to 4 levels under group - dark blue
same level - white
1 to 4 levels higher than group - yellow
5+ levels higher = red
i think averaging the group level is a great idea by the way.

Ahh, yeah I figured this wouldn't work with any custom battle systems. I can easily customize it to fit your color needs, but adapting it to custom battle systems is probably a bit beyond my ability. Especially when i have no clue how they coded it. Also I added the level to the enemy name because it was the only way i could think of to have both display the level difference colors and the HP colors at the same time.
I made some changes for you. I've set up parameters with some preset ranges. Allowing you to choose the color index (\c[x]) Should you choose to ever use the enemy emerges text, and then for the battle screen, you can use hex code to set the text color.
Sorry I can't really adapt this to your battle system, but I think i could probably implement level ranges with scaling stats. I kind of have an idea of how i could make that work.
